Record date: 2128-10-01
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 10/01/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of renal function, and reassessment of mental health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately two weeks after his last visit. He reports a marginal improvement in his respiratory symptoms, particularly in the frequency of nocturnal awakenings, which have decreased to once per night. He continues to utilize his albuterol inhaler three times daily, but he notes that exertional dyspnea persists, especially during stair climbing and walking longer distances. The cough remains present, with occasional sputum production, but he denies any hemoptysis.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains a significant concern, with Mr. Fairfax reporting no substantial change. He describes the swelling as uncomfortable, rating it 6/10, and expresses frustration with the lack of improvement despite strict adherence to sodium restrictions and diuretic therapy. He has gained an additional 2 pounds since the last visit, which raises concerns for worsening fluid retention.
Regarding his mental health, Mr. Fairfax reports a slight decline in mood, attributing this to increased anxiety surrounding his health and the persistent edema. He continues to experience insomnia, with difficulty falling asleep and frequent awakenings throughout the night.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + mild dyspnea, + cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using three times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 160 mg daily (no change). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.4F, HR 76, BP 128/82, RR 20, O2 sat 82% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued and slightly anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.5, Hgb 10.2, Hct 30.5, Plt 220. 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.6, Cl 95, CO2 24, BUN 45, Cr 2.6, Glucose 90. 3. BNP: 700 (slight increase). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax reports minimal improvement in respiratory symptoms. Continue current inhaler regimen. A follow-up pulmonary function test is scheduled for next month to evaluate lung function post-exacerbation. Referral to pulmonary rehabilitation will be initiated to enhance exercise tolerance and improve overall quality of life. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Given the slight increase in serum creatinine, close monitoring of renal function is essential. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema persists with a slight increase in weight. A nephrology referral will be pursued for further evaluation and optimization of diuretic therapy. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and encourage daily weight monitoring. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. A follow-up with psychiatry is scheduled in one week for ongoing management and reassessment of treatment efficacy. Cognitive-behavioral therapy will be explored to address anxiety and insomnia.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
